tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

schema.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
schema.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

Plain output style is active. Remember to follow the specific guidelines for this style.

The sheet shows six candidates in the right column of the welcome screen, and the second image shows candidate C on the full screen with the clip beside it. All of them sit on the layout you chose, with the first-month card on top.

The test I held each line to: a person who has never heard of JusPrin, glancing for two seconds, should come away with three things. What kind of program this is, what the expert inside it does, and why that beats what they do today. The current headline, A, fails the first one. "Your print failed. Ask someone who can see why." is a strong hook, but it never says the word slicer, and a person who has not had a failure this week reads it as an accusation. Its sub line is about the doors, not the proposition, so the whole column has no sentence that says what the product is.

How the others read on the rendered screen:

- **B, "The slicer with a print expert inside."** Names the category first and is calm. It is the safest line, but "expert inside" is a claim anyone can make, and nothing in it says the expert acts. The sub line has to carry the action.
- **C, "A slicer that fixes failed prints."** Six words, one line at the real size, and the verb is "fixes", which is the thing no forum and no other slicer does. The sub line adds the mechanism: show it the photo, it finds the cause in your settings and slices again. This is my pick.
- **D, "Why did my print fail? Now you can ask."** The question is the one people type into Reddit, so it meets them where they are, but it wraps to two lines and "now you can ask" undersells the fix.
- **E, "Expert help for every print. No forum, no waiting."** Two claims and a comparison in one breath. It is the wordiest and reads like a landing page, which is what you called a wall of text.
- **F, "Slice it. Print it. If it fails, ask why."** The rhythm is nice and it puts slicing first, which matches how people will actually use the app. But the payoff is again "ask why" rather than "it fixes it".

Two things I would change regardless of which line you pick. The sub line should state the mechanism in one sentence, as C's does, and the line about choosing how the agent thinks should move down to sit above the doors, where it explains them. And whichever headline wins should not name a specific defect, because the clip beside it already shows one.

The renders and the generator are in `design-captures/value-prop-2026-11/tagline/`, untracked. The animatic session is still working on the two photo versions and will send its welcome screens when done.

Kenneth chose the stringing boat and wants three changes to that clip; drop the too-thick-layers version from further work.

His words: "now it's running too slow. nobody has the patience to wait for it to finish. cut the agent text streaming short. also cut the pause between beats short too." and "the progress bar is not clear that it's slicing. make it clear" and "ideally, we can have a perfectly printed benchy with the same color to replace the stringy version at the end of the slicing progress bar. I think this will make it more obvious, but it's really just a nice to have."

So:
1. Pace. Aim for about 15 s total instead of 25. The streaming text in beat 2 should be a short burst, two or three lines at most, not a paragraph crawl; the two big settings in beat 3 should land within a second of the beat starting; the holds between beats shrink to what it takes to read one caption (about 1.5 s), with only the final frame held longer (about 3 s) before the loop.
2. The slicing bar must read as slicing on its own. Put the word "Slicing…" in large type beside or above the bar, with a percentage or a layer count ticking ("Slicing… layer 143 of 212" or "Slicing… 68 %"), in the app's tokens. Nobody should have to infer it from the caption.
3. Nice to have, do it only if cheap: at the end of the bar, the stringy photo thumbnail is replaced by a clean print of the same boat in the same blue-and-white colours. I am asking the photo session to look for a licensed photo of a clean dual-colour Benchy from the same Flickr account; if one lands at design-captures/value-prop-2026-11/photo/benchy-clean.jpg, use it in beat 4 in place of the sliced preview or beside it, whichever reads clearer at half size. If no photo turns up, keep the sliced preview and say so.

Deliver as before under design-captures/value-prop-2026-11/animatic/: animatic-stringing.mp4 and .gif replacing the current ones, the four beat stills, the welcome composite, the half-size check, and update first-launch-animatic-2026-11.md with the new timeline. content.text:
Yes, I follow. The title has to answer "what is JusPrin" in a glance, and that answer must contain two things: it is a slicer, and an AI does the work. The subtitle is for whoever keeps reading, and that is where the mechanism goes. My earlier set left "AI" out on purpose, because the app's own wording calls it "the agent", but a first-time visitor does not know that word yet. "AI" is the word they already have, so the title should use it and the subtitle can introduce "the agent".

The six new titles all name the AI. Every one sits over the same subtitle, "Show it a photo of what went wrong. The agent reads your file, your settings and your slice, changes the settings and slices again." The line about picking how the agent should think moved down to sit directly above the doors, where it explains them instead of competing with the proposition.

How they read on the screen:

- **A, "The AI slicer that fixes failed prints."** Seven words, one line, and it names the category, the AI and the promise in that order. It is the one a person could repeat to a friend. This is my pick.
- **B, "A slicer with an AI print expert inside."** Also one line and also clear, but "expert inside" describes a feature rather than an outcome, so the subtitle has to do the convincing.
- **C, "An AI agent that slices, and fixes failed prints."** Leads with "agent", which is our word, not theirs, and it wraps to two lines.
- **D, "Slicing with an AI that sees why prints fail."** Says "sees why" instead of "fixes", which undersells what the clip shows, and it wraps.
- **E, "Your AI print expert, built into the slicer."** Warm, but it puts the slicer last and wraps.
- **F, "Slice with AI. Fix failed prints tonight."** The punchiest. Two commands, one line, and "tonight" carries the no-waiting point. Its weakness is that "Slice with AI" alone can read as AI doing the slicing for you, which is a bigger claim than we make.

One thing to watch with A: "AI slicer" is a label other products will use soon, so the second half, "that fixes failed prints", is what keeps it ours. If you want the comparison to forums back in, F is the only one that carries it.

Meanwhile the animatic session re-timed the clip; its welcome composite now samples beat 1 at 2.2 s and the last beat at 11.8 s, so the new cut runs about 12 to 13 s. I will check it when it reports.

Kenneth asks you to revert the no-wizard first-run boards you published (variants A and B) and build the first-run design he has since decided, described in full below.

His words: "tell the design agents to revert the work it did for the no wizard first run flow, and build what we just discussed here."

1. Revert. Take the first-run-a-* and first-run-b-* boards off the "On boarding experience" page of the JusPrin v2 canvas and restore anything on that page you moved or edited to make room for them, so the page is as it was before your variants, plus the new boards below. Keep the builder script, but its page section for A/B goes. Do not touch other pages.

2. What is decided (all on 2026-11-02, by Kenneth, from rendered comparisons; the reference renders are listed at the end):

- Proposition: expert help with a failed print, now, from an AI that can see the person's file, settings and slice and fixes the settings, instead of waiting for a forum reply. Not "simpler slicing".
- No wizard. One welcome screen on first launch, split: a looping silent clip on the LEFT, the words and doors on the RIGHT. Under about 30 words outside the clip.
- Title: "The AI slicer that fixes failed prints." (page-title). Subtitle (body, secondary): "Show it a photo of what went wrong. The agent reads your file, your settings and your slice, changes the settings and slices again."
- A label line directly above the doors: "Pick how the agent should think. Change it any time in Preferences › Agent."
- Doors, weighting "one primary": a selected card "Your first month: 500 credits" / "An Expert message is 5 credits. Then paid, or your own key." / primary button "Sign in for 500 credits"; then two equal slim rows "Your own API key" with cost "Free" and "Claude Code or Claude Desktop" with cost "Free · MCP server"; then the link "Just slice for now". Every free door shows its cost; nothing hidden. Never "trial", no dollar figure. Footer: "Slicing works without an account. The agent needs one, or your own API key."
- The clip, about 12 s, silent, looping, four beats with one caption each: "Show it what happened." / "It reads your photo, your file and your slice." / "It changes the settings for you." / "And slices again. Tonight." Beat 1: the intact 3DBenchy on the plate beside a real photo of a stringing blue-and-white Benchy and the message "I printed it and it failed. What went wrong? Photo attached." Beat 2: a short burst of agent text. Beat 3: two big before→after settings, "Retraction 0.8 → 2 mm" and "Nozzle 220 → 200 °C". Beat 4: a bar labelled "Slicing NN%" counting up; at 100 % the stringy thumbnail fades to a clean print of the same boat, a green check pops, and "Sliced · ready · 1 h 34 min · 34 g". Motion only at beat changes, short holds, last frame held longest.
- After the doors, nothing new is decided: each setup door opens Preferences › Agent as the 2026-10-23 one-flow decision says, and "Just slice for now" goes to Home with the printer order Kenneth decided earlier (3MF preset, else OrcaSlicer import, else a default the chip marks as assumed). Reuse your existing after-door boards only where they already match that; where they don't, leave them out and list the gap in your note rather than inventing a screen.

3. Boards to publish on that page, as whole screens at the app's size, built from the token file through the usual recipes (no literals): the welcome screen with the clip at beat 1; the welcome screen with the clip at the final frame (the one peripheral vision sees most); and one storyboard board of the four clip beats with their captions. Strings are exactly the ones above; the agent's words in beat 2 are placeholders until a live run and the board should say so in a small note.

4. Reference renders, all untracked under /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/design-captures/value-prop-2026-11/: tagline/ai-a-ai-slicer.png (the welcome with the chosen title, clip at beat 1), animatic/welcome-stringing.png (the composite with the live clip), animatic/beats/stringing-beat-{1,2,3,4a,4}-*.png (the beat stills), animatic/animatic-stringing.mp4 (the clip), photo/benchy-stringing.jpg and photo/benchy-clean.jpg with photo/ATTRIBUTION.md (CC BY 2.0; the credit must appear somewhere, so put a small credit line on the storyboard board). The decision record is in memory at ~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/first-run-value-prop-decisions.md. Update your note first-run-flow-design-2026-11.md at the repo root to say A/B are withdrawn and what replaced them; keep it untracked, commit nothing.

When done, report the canvas version, the board names, and anything you left out, and send a PNG of the welcome board with SendUserFile.

## Logo use

The primary expressions are the horizontal lockup, the compact product mark, and the text wordmark. Use the compact mark for application icons and small product contexts.

- Clear space: at least one quarter of the mark width on every side.
- Minimum digital mark: 24 px.
- Minimum digital horizontal lockup: 120 px.
- Minimum printed mark: 8 mm.
- Minimum printed lockup: 32 mm.
- Below these sizes, use the mark alone and verify that the orbit arcs remain distinct.

Always use the original artwork, preserve its aspect ratio and components, maintain clear space, and place it on White, Mist, Ink, or another quiet solid field. Do not stretch, rotate, redraw, arbitrarily recolor, outline, shadow, separate, or place it directly over visual noise. Monochrome is allowed only when required. If the center crossing or orbit loses clarity, increase size, contrast, or space.

## Brand palette

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---:|---|
| Orbit | `#3A2D64` | Primary brand color and decisive light-mode action |
| Violet | `#6F4F84` | Secondary brand color, headings, and essential boundaries |
| Bloom | `#CE84B7` | Expressive accent and dark-mode primary action |
| Ink | `#17131F` | Primary text and dark canvas |
| Mist | `#F6F2F7` | Soft canvas and grouped surfaces |
| Trace | `#E8DFEB` | Light dividers and quiet structure |
| White | `#FFFFFF` | Primary light canvas |
| Success | `#2D6A55` | Light success state |
| Danger | `#B44757` | Light error or destructive state |
| Warning | `#D49A2A` | Light warning state |

content.text:
Taking the four in order.

**1. The logo.** There is no decision against it. It was an omission: my render generators started from the app's standing shell header, which carries the word "JusPrin" as a text breadcrumb, and the welcome inherited that. The design system actually argues the other way. It reserves the brand gradient for "splash, onboarding, and rare hero moments" and says never to use it as ordinary chrome, so this screen is the one place the original mark is meant to appear. The artwork is in the repo under `resources/jusprin/branding/`. My recommendation is the horizontal lockup, mark plus wordmark, at the top of the right column above the title, at least 120 px wide with its clear space, on the plain canvas. That reads as "this is JusPrin" once and then gets out of the way. The alternative is the mark alone at about 40 px, which is quieter but makes the wordmark do double duty with the title.

**2. The header and footer.** You are right that they distract, and the header is worse than distracting. It is the app shell's breadcrumb and agent status, so on this screen it says "Agent › Agent not connected" before the person has chosen anything, which reads like an error on first launch. The welcome should be a full-window screen with no shell chrome. The footer sentence was mine, to say slicing is free without an account. The door rows already show "Free" twice and "Just slice for now" implies the rest, so it goes too. With both gone, the only words on the screen are the title, the subtitle, the agent-choice line, the doors and the clip captions.

**3. Importing OrcaSlicer profiles.** Agreed, and there is a precedent in the code. The app already imports a JusPrin v1 setup on first launch: it copies the user presets, printer connections and preferences from v1's folder before OrcaSlicer reads anything, then shows a one-time "welcome back" screen listing what came along. An OrcaSlicer import can reuse that machinery, because v1's folder is OrcaSlicer's format. The one difference I would make is consent. The v1 copy is silent because it is our own product's data; OrcaSlicer's folder belongs to another program, and the copy includes printer access codes, so it should be asked, not assumed. That gives the answer to where: a conditional screen right after the door, shown only when an OrcaSlicer folder exists on the machine, saying something like "OrcaSlicer is on this Mac with 3 printers and 14 filaments. Bring them in?" with Import and Start fresh. People who skip it, or who install OrcaSlicer later, get the same action as a row in Home's Printers column and in the add-printer form. It does not belong on the welcome itself, which must stay under 30 words.

**4. Follow-up screens.** Yes, the welcome is only the first screen. What follows depends on the door, and most of it already exists:

- **Sign in for 500 credits** opens the browser sign-in, returns to the app, then the conditional OrcaSlicer screen, then Home with the agent connected and the 500-credit balance shown once. The credits boards on the canvas cover that balance.
- **Your own API key** opens Preferences › Agent on the key field, per the one-flow decision from 2026-10-23, verifies the key, then the OrcaSlicer screen, then Home.
- **Claude Code or Claude Desktop** opens Preferences › Agent on the MCP section with the config to paste, then Home.
- **Just slice for now** goes to the OrcaSlicer screen if applicable, then Home with the agent column offering the same three doors in a collapsed form, so the choice is still one click away later.

Two screens are missing from the canvas today, both flagged by the design session: Home as it looks right after "Just slice for now", and the printer chip marked as an assumed default when there is no 3MF preset and no OrcaSlicer to import from. The code finding behind the second one still stands: the "from the file" rule cannot tell an assumed default apart, so the mark needs a stored origin. There is also a separate existing path for v1 users, the welcome-back window, which runs before any of this and should stay as it is.

Both renders are attached. The shell header with its breadcrumb and agent status is gone, and so is the footer sentence, so the only words on the screen are the title, the subtitle, the agent-choice line, the doors and the clip's caption.

The first render carries the horizontal lockup, mark plus wordmark, above the title. I sized it at the design system's minimum lockup width, which puts it just above the title with its own clear space. The second carries the mark alone at 40 px in the same spot. Both use the original artwork from the branding folder with the gradient intact, which the design system reserves for exactly this kind of screen.

My pick is the lockup. The mark alone is quieter, but the orbit-and-cross shape does not yet say "JusPrin" to someone seeing it for the first time, and the wordmark is what makes the title read as this product's claim rather than a generic headline. Either way the logo now sits once on the screen and nowhere else, which answers your earlier worry about it being in people's faces.

Once you pick, the canvas boards need the same three changes: the logo added, the header and footer removed. That is a small message to the design session, which has the boards.

Agreed, and the evidence says the same. I captured the live first screen of twelve products tonight with a headless browser. Slack blocked it, Bambu's wiki page was gone and Prusa's page is an article, so nine count. They are attached as a sheet and saved in `design-captures/value-prop-2026-11/logo-refs/`.

Two patterns cover all nine:

- **Centred column, small mark above the title.** Notion, Linear, GitHub and Spotify put a mark of roughly 24 to 32 px, no wordmark, centred above a short title, with lots of air above it. The logo is part of the content stack, and it is small.
- **Split or branded layout, wordmark anchored top-left of the window.** Stripe, Dropbox, Zoom, Canva and Figma put the wordmark or mark in the top-left corner at text height, in a slim band or on its own, and keep the content centred below. The logo is a corner anchor, not part of the content column.

Nobody puts a lockup inside the content column at display size, which is what my two earlier renders did. That is why they looked wrong: the logo competed with the title for the same spot and the same weight.

Our screen is a split layout, so it follows the second pattern. The two new renders put the logo top-left of the whole window and leave the content untouched:

- **Mark plus text at 24 px.** The mark with "JusPrin" set in the app's section style, the same size Stripe and Dropbox use. My pick. It reads as the window's name, which is what a corner logo is for, and the gradient mark is still there.
- **Lockup at its minimum width.** The original artwork at 43 px tall. Heavier, closer to Zoom's, and the only version where the design system's lockup rule is satisfied.

Whichever you choose, the canvas boards need the same three edits: the corner logo added, the shell header and the footer sentence removed. That is one message to the design session.

Here is where each path after the welcome stands:

- **Sign in for 500 credits.** The sign-in itself happens in the browser, so no board. The credits boards show balances, but none shows this first return, and the existing setup board's offer wording has not been checked against the new card's line "Then paid, or your own key."

- **The OrcaSlicer import.** No board. This is the conditional screen right after any door, shown only when an OrcaSlicer folder exists, with Import and Start fresh.
- **Coming from JusPrin v1.** The welcome-back window exists in the code and has its own boards. Covered.

So four screens are missing: the OrcaSlicer import, Home after sign-in, Home after "Just slice" with the assumed printer, and a check of the credits setup board's wording. All four are small, since Home and Preferences › Agent already have their design, and each is one state of an existing screen plus one new dialog-sized screen.

content.text:
You're right, I described destinations and skipped the transitions. I checked two facts in the code before redoing it: the Preferences window is modal and hands control back when it closes, and the browser sign-in returns to the app through a loopback callback the app polls, so the app knows the moment it finishes. Both detours can therefore return to a flow that owns the steps.

**The shape.** Onboarding is a short sequence, Welcome → Printers → Home, and the agent doors are detours off step 1, never exits. A controller owns the current step. Dialogs and the browser are detours: when one closes, the controller decides what comes next. Nothing a detour does can strand the person outside the sequence.

**Step 1, Welcome.** The screen we designed. Each door behaves differently:

- **Sign in for 500 credits.** The browser opens. The card itself changes to a waiting state: "Finish signing in in your browser" with a Cancel link, the other doors dimmed. When the callback arrives, the card flips to "Signed in as k@obico.io · 500 credits" for a beat, then the controller advances to step 2. Cancel, or closing the browser tab, puts the card back as it was. Nothing else on the screen moves, so a person who changes their mind is still on the welcome.
- **Your own API key** and **Claude Code or Claude Desktop.** Preferences › Agent opens as the modal window it already is, on the right section, over the welcome. Saving a verified key, or Done on the MCP section, closes it and the controller advances to step 2. Closing it without finishing returns to the welcome with nothing chosen. Preferences never navigates anywhere itself. It only closes.
- **Just slice for now.** Advances to step 2 at once. This is the case you asked about: skipping the agent does not skip onboarding, it skips one detour.

**Step 2, Printers.** The app needs at least one printer, because an empty data folder has none. The step shows one of three screens, decided by what the app finds:

- **OrcaSlicer is on this machine.** "Bring your printers from OrcaSlicer?" listing its printers and filament count, with Import and Start fresh. Import copies the user presets the way the v1 import already does, then goes to Home. Start fresh goes to the add-printer screen below.
- **JusPrin v1 is on this machine.** The v1 import already ran silently at launch, so this step is skipped and the existing welcome-back window shows over Home instead.
- **Neither.** The existing add-printer form, search by model, with a "Skip, use a default" link. Skip installs the default printer and marks the chip as assumed, which is your printer-order decision.

A Back link on this step returns to the welcome. Anything done there stays done: a signed-in card shows signed in, a saved key stays saved. A 3MF opened by double-click on first launch still shows the welcome, then skips this step because the file carries its printer, and the chip says "from the file".

**Step 3, Home.** The first-run Home state reflects the choices: the agent column shows the connection and, after sign-in, the 500 credits once; or, after Just slice, the same three doors collapsed into the column with "Set up the agent" so the choice stays one click away. The Printers column lists what was imported, added or assumed.

**Quitting mid-flow.** The onboarding is marked done only when Home is reached. Quitting earlier shows the welcome again next launch, with any finished detour reflected on its card.

**What this adds to the canvas.** Four new states and one new screen: the welcome's waiting and signed-in card states, the OrcaSlicer import screen, the add-printer form with its skip link, and Home after sign-in and after Just slice with the assumed chip. Plus the old wizard boards on the same page, which should be marked superseded. One flow diagram board tying the steps together would stop the next person from making my mistake.

---
name: first-run-flow-sequence
description: "Kenneth's 2026-11-02 first-run flow after the welcome: a sequence Welcome → Printers → Home owned by a controller, with the agent doors as detours that return (sign-in waits on the card, Preferences closes back, Just slice skips the detour not the sequence); Printers step imports OrcaSlicer or adds/assumes a printer; what the canvas still lacks."
metadata:
  type: project
---

Decided 2026-11-02, late, after Kenneth asked how Preferences gets back to the OrcaSlicer import and how "Just slice for now" returns to onboarding ("I don't think you have thought through").

- **Shape:** onboarding is a sequence, Welcome → Printers → Home. A controller owns the step. Preferences (a modal `PreferencesWindow`, returns on close) and the browser sign-in (loopback callback on port 41172, polled by `CloudSignIn::poll()`) are detours off step 1; when one finishes the controller advances. Nothing a detour does strands the person outside the sequence.
- **Welcome doors:** Sign in → browser; the card shows "Finish signing in in your browser" with Cancel, other doors dimmed; on the callback the card flips to "Signed in as … · 500 credits", then step 2. Own key / MCP → Preferences › Agent opens modal on that section; saving a verified key or Done closes it and advances; closing unfinished returns to the welcome with nothing chosen. Just slice → step 2 at once.
- **Printers step:** the app needs one printer (an empty data folder has none). OrcaSlicer folder found → "Bring your printers from OrcaSlicer?" with Import (copies user presets like `V1Import`, but asked, not silent) and Start fresh. JusPrin v1 found → step skipped, the existing welcome-back window shows over Home. Neither → the add-printer form with "Skip, use a default", which installs the default and marks the chip assumed. Back returns to the welcome; finished detours stay done. A 3MF opened on first launch still shows the welcome, then skips this step ("from the file").
- **Home:** first-run state reflects the choices: agent connected and the 500 credits shown once, or the three doors collapsed in the agent column after Just slice; the Printers column lists imported/added/assumed.
- **Quit mid-flow:** done is marked only when Home is reached; next launch shows the welcome again with finished detours reflected.

**Why:** the first design named destinations and skipped transitions; Kenneth wants every door to come back into one flow.

**How to apply:** build the controller first, then the screens; the canvas needs the welcome's waiting and signed-in card states, the OrcaSlicer import screen, the add-printer form with skip, Home after sign-in and after Just slice, a flow board, and the old wizard boards marked superseded. Related: [[first-run-value-prop-decisions]], [[first-run-flow-boards]], [[agent-setup-one-flow-decisions]].
EOF

p='MEMORY.md'; s=open(p).read()
line='- [First-run sequence](first-run-flow-sequence.md) — Welcome → Printers → Home; doors are returning detours; Printers imports Orca or adds/assumes; canvas gaps.\n'
anchor='- [First-run proposition]'
s=s.replace(anchor, line+anchor,1); open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
grep -c 'First-run sequence' MEMORY.md

The flow is below in full; it is also in memory at ~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/first-run-flow-sequence.md.

THE FLOW. Onboarding is a sequence, Welcome → Printers → Home, owned by a controller. The agent doors on the welcome are detours that return into the sequence, never exits. Two code facts make that possible and must be stated on the flow board: the Preferences window is modal and hands control back when it closes (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Preferences/PreferencesWindow.hpp), and the browser sign-in returns through a loopback callback the app polls (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/CloudAccount.hpp, port 41172).

Step 1, Welcome (boards 01/02 as they are). Door behaviour:
- Sign in for 500 credits: the browser opens. The offer card changes to a waiting state: "Finish signing in in your browser" with a Cancel link; the two free rows and "Just slice for now" are dimmed. When the callback arrives the card flips to "Signed in as kenneth@example.com · 500 credits" (use a placeholder address, never a real one) and the controller advances to step 2. Cancel puts the card back as it was.
- Your own API key / Claude Code or Claude Desktop: Preferences › Agent opens modal on that section over the welcome. Saving a verified key, or Done on the MCP section, closes it and advances to step 2. Closing it unfinished returns to the welcome with nothing chosen. Preferences never navigates; it only closes.
- Just slice for now: advances to step 2 at once. It skips the detour, not the sequence.

Step 2, Printers. The app needs at least one printer (an empty data folder has none). One of three screens, decided by what the app finds:
- OrcaSlicer folder on this machine: "Bring your printers from OrcaSlicer?" listing its printers by name and a filament count, with Import (primary) and Start fresh. Import copies the user presets the way the v1 import does, but asked rather than silent, because the folder belongs to another program and includes printer access codes. Then Home. Start fresh goes to the add-printer screen.
- JusPrin v1 on this machine: step skipped; the existing welcome-back window shows over Home (already designed, onboarding-v1-01…03).
- Neither: the existing add-printer form (search by model, merged f073fdba96) as this step, with a "Skip, use a default" link that installs the default printer and marks the chip as assumed.
- A Back link on this step returns to the welcome; anything finished there stays finished (the card shows signed in, a saved key stays saved).
- A 3MF opened by double-click on first launch still shows the welcome, then skips this step because the file carries its printer; the chip says "from the file".

Step 3, Home, first-run state reflecting the choices:
- After sign-in: the agent column shows the connection and the 500-credit balance once (reuse the credits boards' balance treatment).
- After Just slice: the same three doors collapsed into the agent column under "Set up the agent", so the choice stays one click away.
- The Printers column lists what was imported, added, or the assumed default with its mark.
Onboarding is marked done only when Home is reached; quitting earlier shows the welcome again next launch with finished detours reflected on its card.

04 welcome, sign-in waiting state; 05 welcome, signed-in card just before advancing; 06 Preferences › Agent modal over the welcome, key section (reuse the prefs boards); 07 OrcaSlicer import screen; 08 add-printer step with the skip link; 09 Home after sign-in; 10 Home after Just slice with the collapsed doors and the assumed chip; 11 a flow board: the three steps as boxes, each door's path as an arrow that returns to step 2, the three Printers branches, Back, and the quit rule, with the two code facts as footnotes. Keep the three welcome boards as they are.

The old wizard boards (onboarding-00 to -20) contradict this flow. Do not delete them; add one note beside them saying they are superseded by first-run-01…11 as of 2026-11-02, and move them to the bottom of the page if the builder allows.

Reference: the printer-order decision and the chip-origin finding are in your own note; the credits balance treatment is on the credits boards. Publish, update design-captures/first-run-2026-11/ and first-run-flow-design-2026-11.md, commit nothing, and send the flow board PNG and board 07 with SendUserFile when done, with the canvas version and anything you left out.
